sources.title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = lambda W
sources.content: John D. C. Little's 1961 Operations Research paper proves L=lambda W under finite-mean, stationary, and transitivity conditions. The relation uses mean W; a latency percentile cannot be substituted for the mean without a separate derivation.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.content: Official SQLite documentation describes WAL mode, the separate WAL and shared-memory files, automatic and application-initiated checkpoints, and the concurrency boundary. It supports the measured runtime description, not a claim about a multi-host database.

sources.title: Python time.perf_counter_ns
sources.content: The Python documentation defines perf_counter_ns as a high-resolution monotonic performance counter returned as integer nanoseconds; only differences between readings are meaningful. On the measured Windows environment it uses QueryPerformanceCounter.

sources.title: Service Level Objectives
sources.content: Google's SRE chapter distinguishes measured service-level indicators from target SLOs, recommends percentiles over means for tail behavior, and requires the measurement conditions and population to be specified. It also warns against choosing a public target from current performance alone.

claims.text: The timestamped local benchmark completed 1728 paced ToolGateway events across 10, 34, and 100 events/s, with three cold and three warm trials per load and a deterministic seed of 20260824.
At the 34 events/s planning point, cold end-to-end latency was mean 3.436 ms, p95 4.262 ms, p99 5.295 ms, queue depth max 0; warm was mean 4.008 ms, p95 5.221 ms, p99 11.511 ms, queue depth max 0.
At 100 events/s, cold p95/p99 end-to-end latency was 4.272/7.392 ms with max queue depth 1; warm p95/p99 was 4.762/7.533 ms with max queue depth 1 and single-worker mean busy ratio 0.317.
A separate 2000-invocation storage probe added 4000 persisted rows and 1413120 bytes after WAL checkpoint, measuring 353.28 bytes per persisted row for this schema and payload.
Little's Law relates long-run mean occupancy, arrival rate, and mean time as L=lambda W under its stated conditions; it does not license replacing mean W with p95.
The measured single-process SQLite/WAL path has local headroom at 34 and 100 events/s in this bounded workload, but the result does not validate a distributed worker count or production capacity.

The SRC-06 numeric profile is a planning input whose agents, external-call rate, worker count, revocation, fan-out, and production storage assumptions remain unverified outside the explicitly measured local path.
Retain p95 authorization latency below 20 ms as an internal target for later representative benchmarks, not as a production SLO or customer commitment.

research_plan.content:
# Question
Do the planning values around 34 events/s, a 20 ms p95 target, 100 events/s bursts, worker count, and annual storage survive a reproducible local workload, and what remains unverified?

# Method
Benchmark the actual read-only AgentOS ToolGateway path: registry resolution, schema validation, 90/10 seeded capability allow/deny, handler, activity persistence, and hash-chained audit event. Use CPython perf_counter_ns, fixed-rate arrivals at 10/34/100 events/s, 2 seconds per trial, three trials per rate, separate zero-warmup cold and 100-event warm modes, and seed 20260824. Record raw event latency, mean, standard deviation, p50/p95/p99/max, queue wait/depth, busy ratio, timestamps, environment, and storage growth.

# Evidence boundary
Raw record: research/tickets/stage-1/S1-002/raw-results.json, 552600 bytes, SHA-256 8cf8e60290d5992f1a495a700b7bc812ccf2ea725c75822a23104c94918d9d3f. Script: research/tickets/stage-1/S1-002/benchmark.py.

# Non-scope
No network/model latency, multi-process or multi-host workers, production traffic, failover, multi-region reliability, or public SLO.

# Stop rule
Stop if timestamps, raw observations, percentiles, queue measures, environment, or workload seed cannot be captured; reject any request to publish these local results as a production SLO.

source_registry.content:
# Evidence classes
1. Mathematical: Little 1961 for L=lambda W and its mean/stationarity conditions. 2. Runtime architecture: official SQLite WAL documentation. 3. Benchmark method: Python perf_counter_ns and Google SRE percentile/SLO guidance. 4. Empirical: the checked-in timestamped raw-results.json generated by benchmark.py.

# Local empirical record
Path: research/tickets/stage-1/S1-002/raw-results.json. SHA-256: 8cf8e60290d5992f1a495a700b7bc812ccf2ea725c75822a23104c94918d9d3f. Schema: agentos.s1-002-benchmark/v1. Run: 2026-08-24T17:52:01.458Z through 2026-08-24T17:52:47.550Z. Environment: AgentOS 950cd4d, CPython 3.11.15, SQLite 3.53.1, Windows 10 build 22631, 16 logical CPUs, WAL, QueryPerformanceCounter resolution 1e-7 s.

# Status
External method sources are verified. The empirical file is measured local evidence. It is not elevated to production evidence and is not represented as an externally hosted source.

feature_catalog.content:
# Capacity evidence feature
A benchmark run must carry workload rates, arrival model, allowed/denied mix, duration, trials, seed, warmup definition, worker count, environment, start/end timestamps, raw event observations, aggregate distributions, queue metrics, and storage checkpoint policy.

# Downstream use
S1-004 may consume the arrival/service observations for simulation; S1-005 and S1-006 may use the bounded local headroom only as topology/backend input; S1-008 must independently measure revocation; S1-019 may cite the result only with the single-process/local boundary.

# Labels
Domain labels map into the harness as measurement=fact, design_inference=inference, planning_assumption or uncertainty=assumption, and SLO_target=target.

architecture_models.content:
# Measured path
Fixed-rate scheduler -> ToolGateway.invoke -> authoritative ToolContract resolve in SQLite -> argument validation -> capability allow/deny -> read handler when allowed -> one activity row -> one hash-chained audit_event row.

# Runtime topology
One CPython process, one SQLite connection, WAL mode, one logical workload worker, no network. Each measured gateway invocation adds one activity and one audit row. The 2000-invocation storage probe therefore adds 4000 rows.

# Boundary
This validates a local control-plane slice, not engine scheduling, external calls, parallel connections, durable distributed execution, model latency, or multi-region storage. A later backend benchmark must preserve the same event schema and workload seed while adding representative concurrency.

mental_model.content:
# Operator view
Every number is shown with a badge: MEASURED, DERIVED, TARGET, or UNVERIFIED. The view must display environment and workload beside latency; p95/p99 and queue depth are primary, while mean is retained for Little's Law.

# Interpretation
'Observed below 20 ms locally' is not '20 ms production SLO achieved'. At 100 events/s, warm p95 was 4.762 ms and p99 7.533 ms, yet an individual maximum reached 25.260 ms and the run lasted only 2 seconds per trial.

# Decision cue
Use the result to approve a larger representative benchmark, not to publish capacity. Surface missing dimensions: concurrent processes, network, realistic payloads, external effects, sustained duration, failure injection, revocation, backup/replica overhead, and production hardware variance.

ontology.content:
# Evidence value classes
MeasuredValue: directly observed in a named run with unit, distribution, timestamp, environment, seed, and raw reference. DerivedValue: computed from measured or explicitly named assumed inputs and formula. TargetValue: desired future threshold with no claim that it is currently guaranteed. UnverifiedValue: planning input not measured in the scoped run.

# Entities
BenchmarkRun, WorkloadLevel, Trial, RawObservation, AggregateDistribution, EnvironmentSnapshot, QueueMetric, UtilizationMetric, StorageProbe, Projection, SLOTarget, and Limitation.

# Relations
Trial partOf BenchmarkRun; RawObservation observedIn Trial; AggregateDistribution derivedFrom RawObservation; Projection derivedFrom Measurement or Assumption; SLOTarget evaluatedBy future BenchmarkRun.

# Invariants
A measured latency includes clock and population. A percentile includes sample count and workload. A projection names every assumption. A production SLO cannot be inferred from a local BenchmarkRun.

# Little's Law
Using mean end-to-end W only: at 34/s, L_local is derived as 34*0.003436=0.117 cold and 34*0.004008=0.136 warm. At 100/s warm it is 100*0.003705=0.371. These are bounded local occupancy estimates, not worker-pool proof. The historical 0.68 value is derived from the target 34*0.020 and remains a target-based estimate.

# Storage
Measured after checkpoint: 2000 gateway invocations -> 2000 activity + 2000 audit rows; delta 1413120 bytes; 706.56 bytes/invocation and 353.28 bytes/persisted row. Derived projection at 36.5M rows is 12.009 GiB for this exact local payload/schema. The historical 1 KiB/row projection is derived as 34.809 GiB. Neither includes future indexes, backups, replicas, artifacts, or filesystem allocation.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Result
The 34/s planning point and 100/s burst were both sustained by the bounded local path in all six aggregate scenarios. Warm 34/s p95 was 5.221 ms with queue max 0; warm 100/s p95/p99 was 4.762/7.533 ms with queue max 1 and mean busy ratio 0.317. This supports local implementation headroom and preserves the 20 ms value only as a future internal target.

# Storage result
The measured schema/payload used 353.28 bytes per added activity/audit row after checkpoint, yielding a derived 12.009 GiB at 36.5M rows versus the planning 34.809 GiB at 1 KiB/row. The lower local value is not a production forecast.

# Gaps
Trials were short (2 seconds), fixed-rate and single-process; the workload used a tiny read handler, one SQLite connection, no network/model/external call, no failure injection, and no representative artifact/index/backup overhead. M/M/c assumptions and c=4 are not validated. Revocation, fan-out, and sustained burst behavior remain open.

# Recommendation
Carry the measured distributions into S1-004 simulation and use them as a baseline for S1-005/S1-006. Before any production SLO, run longer randomized and bursty arrivals with multiple processes/connections, representative payloads, external dependencies, failure injection, hardware controls, and confidence intervals.

independent_audit.content:
# Integrity review
The verifier recomputed the raw-results SHA-256 as 8cf8e60290d5992f1a495a700b7bc812ccf2ea725c75822a23104c94918d9d3f and checked 18 timestamped trials: 3 rates * 2 modes * 3 trials, totaling 1728 paced observations. The 2000-event storage probe is separate.

# Probe 1: assumption-only report
A synthetic report containing only '34 events/s' with no timestamp, raw record, seed, environment, or distribution is classified TARGET/UNVERIFIED and cannot support capacity. PASS: this bundle instead includes all required provenance and raw observations.

# Probe 2: mean-only burst
A synthetic 100/s report containing only mean latency is rejected. PASS: cold and warm results include p95, p99, max, queue wait/depth, utilization, achieved rate, and raw events.

# Adversarial findings
The local 20 ms observation cannot be generalized to production. Maximum latency exceeded 20 ms in the 34/s warm and 100/s cold/warm aggregates even though p95 stayed below target. Little's Law calculations use mean W, not p95. The lower storage result excludes major production overhead.

# Verdict
PASS_WITH_LIMITS. The measured claims and both probes pass for the local baseline. Limits: short single-process runs, deterministic arrivals, non-representative handler/payload, no external independent human/model auditor, and no production SLO authority.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope
Preserve this run as the local control-plane baseline and build the next benchmark layer; do not change production architecture or publish an SLO from S1-002 alone.

# Architecture
Keep a versioned benchmark runner beside each ticket bundle, raw JSON with environment/seed/timestamps, immutable SHA binding in FLOW artifacts, and a common result schema. Add adapters for multiple processes/connections and external dependency stubs without changing the canonical gateway contract.

# Workstreams
1. Add sustained and bursty arrival profiles. 2. Add representative payload size classes and allow/deny/approval paths. 3. Add multi-process SQLite and candidate durable-backend comparisons. 4. Add network/external-call stubs with controlled latency/failure distributions. 5. Measure checkpoint, backup, index, and artifact storage. 6. Feed distributions into S1-004 and backend choices into S1-005/S1-006.

# Milestones
M1 preserves the current reproducible baseline. M2 runs 15-minute sustained profiles with confidence intervals. M3 adds burst/failure and multi-process matrices. M4 compares candidate execution backends under identical seeds. M5 proposes an internal SLO with workload and hardware boundaries for review.

# Verification
Require at least three loads including 34/s and 100/s, cold/warm separation, p95/p99/max, achieved rate, queue wait/depth, utilization, timestamps, seed, raw hashes, environment, storage checkpoint method, and near-miss probes. Compare repeated runs and fail on missing tail or queue data.

# Risks
Timer/scheduler noise, short samples, cache state, WAL checkpoint behavior, payload drift, a single connection masking contention, hardware variance, coordinated omission, and treating local headroom as production evidence.

# Open decisions
Choose sustained duration and confidence method; define realistic arrival distributions and payload corpus; select concurrency levels; decide whether SQLite or a durable backend is the comparison target after S1-005; name the independent auditor and deployment envelope required before an SLO proposal.

progress.content:
# 2026-08-24
S1-002 benchmark runner authored and executed twice. The first pass exposed the need for mean W; the final pass added mean and population standard deviation while preserving p50/p95/p99/max. Final raw run: 2026-08-24T17:52:01.458Z to 2026-08-24T17:52:47.550Z, 1728 paced events plus 2000 storage-probe events, seed 20260824.

Final raw path: research/tickets/stage-1/S1-002/raw-results.json; bytes 552600; SHA-256 8cf8e60290d5992f1a495a700b7bc812ccf2ea725c75822a23104c94918d9d3f. All six load/mode aggregates include p95/p99 and queue depth.

Current research decision: PASS_WITH_LIMITS pending canonical research-plan persistence and wiki check. No production SLO, distributed worker count, revocation bound, or annual production storage claim is closed by this run.

limitations: The benchmark is a short single-process local SQLite/WAL baseline with deterministic arrivals and a small read handler, not production traffic.
Distributed worker count, external calls, revocation, fan-out, failover, and multi-region behavior remain unverified.
The auditor role is adversarial and process-separated but not an external human or independently operated model.
The 20 ms p95 value remains an internal target; no production SLO or customer commitment is authorized.
